title: 3D ULPIN Generation and vertical Property Mapping SYstem
description:
Background:
With rapid urbanization and vertical growth of cities, conventional 2D land record Systems are becoming inadequate for managing modern urban properties.Existing land administration systems are primarily designed to identify surface-level land parcels and are unable to uniquely define ownership rights associated with multi- storey apartments, underground infrastructure, elevated transport corridors, parking spaces, air-rights, and subsurface utility networks.
Description:
The proposed solution Should develop an advanced 3D ULPIN(Unique Land Parcel ldentification Number) Generation and vertical Property Mapping system capable of creating unique spatial identities for:
. Surface land parcels . Multi-storey apartments . Underground infrastructure The system should integrate:
. Drone imagery . LiDAR/3D Point cloud data . GIS parcel layers . Building floor Plans . GNSS/CORS-based coordinates . Digital Elevation Models (DEM/DSM) The solution should also incorporate AI/ML capabilities for:
. Automated building extraction . Floor segmentation . Vertical Parcel delineation . lntelligent topology validation Expected Solution: The expected outcome is development of a scalable and interoperable 3D cadastral framework capable of:
. Generating standardized 3D ULPINs . Mapping vertical and underground ownership rights . Supporting volumetric cadastre systems . Enabling accurate urban property governance . Reducing ownership conflicts and ambiguities . lmproving infrastructure planning and utility management
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, drone applied to a space technology problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (4/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a working prototype is realistic in a 36-hour window. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Space Technology. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on gis, infrastructure. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 22/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: 3D ULPIN Generation and vertical Property Mapping System

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that gives every layer of a modern building, floors, basements, parking, underground utilities, its own unique property ID, so land records finally work for vertical cities, not just flat plots.
overview.why_it_matters: Current land records can't tell you who owns the 14th floor apartment versus the basement parking spot, that's a real gap as cities grow vertically. This closes it.
pain_points: 2D land records can't represent ownership in multi-storey buildings.
Underground infrastructure and air-rights have no unique identification system.
No standardized way to generate 3D property IDs from available spatial data.
overview.background: As cities grow vertically, 2D land record systems can't represent ownership of apartments, underground infrastructure, or elevated structures, a structural gap in current cadastral systems.
overview.whats_being_asked: A 3D ULPIN generation system integrating drone imagery, LiDAR, GIS layers, building plans, GNSS coordinates, and elevation models, with AI for automated building extraction and floor segmentation.
expected_solution: 3D ULPIN generation for surface, multi-storey, and underground parcels.
AI-based building extraction and floor segmentation.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. 3D cadastral systems are a genuinely emerging area globally, this isn't incremental, it's building a new representation format for property ownership.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate-high. LiDAR/3D point cloud processing is specialized; a scaled-down demo using building floor plans plus 2D-to-3D approximation is far more tractable than full LiDAR integration.

competitive_landscape.note: Part of the same Ministry of Rural Development land-records cluster as SIH26010/12/13/14, differentiate by focusing specifically on the vertical/3D angle other PS in this cluster don't cover.

innovation.note: 3D cadastral representation is a genuinely emerging concept, not a rehash of existing 2D land record digitization.

invention.note: Full LiDAR/point-cloud pipeline is heavy, but a floor-plan-based approximation of vertical parcels is a reasonable, lighter-weight path to the same core idea.

technical_feasibility.tag: Workable if scoped to floor plans, Tight if full LiDAR
technical_feasibility.note: Real LiDAR data and drone imagery for a specific building aren't accessible to most teams; building-plan-based 3D approximation is achievable.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly useful mainly for urban vertical property administration, less immediately dramatic than disaster/health PS but genuinely important as cities grow.

architecture.note: Multiple spatial data types feeding a unique-ID generation system, manageable if you don't chase full LiDAR fidelity.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with GIS/3D modeling interest. The floor-plan-approximation path makes this genuinely buildable while still demonstrating the core novel idea, unique 3D property identity.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: A genuinely novel, forward-looking cadastral concept, most competing land-records PS this cycle are 2D digitization, this one is conceptually different.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Chasing full LiDAR/point-cloud fidelity instead of a building-plan-based approximation will eat all 36 hours on data processing alone, with nothing to show.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm you're building from architectural floor plans (accessible) rather than committing to real LiDAR/drone data capture (not accessible in 36 hours) before starting.

idea_0_4: Commit to building from floor plans/building schematics rather than real LiDAR data, this is the single most important scope decision.
Design your 3D ULPIN format/schema, what makes each vertical parcel's ID unique and structured.
Split: one person on ID generation logic, one on 3D visualization.
prototype_4_22: Build the parcel-ID generation logic from a sample building's floor plan data.
Build a basic 3D visualization showing distinct floors/units as separate identified parcels.
Handle the underground/parking-space case as a distinct parcel type.
integration_22_30: Connect ID generation to the visualization, clicking a floor/unit shows its unique ULPIN and ownership metadata.
Test with a multi-building scenario to confirm ID uniqueness holds.
Add basic topology validation (no overlapping or duplicate parcel definitions).
polish_30_36: Polish the 3D visualization for demo impact, this is a visually compelling PS if executed well.
Rehearse explaining the floor-plan-based approach honestly as a scoped proof of concept for the full LiDAR vision.
Prepare to explain how this would integrate with existing 2D ULPIN systems.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Build a genuinely interactive 3D visualization, click a floor, see its unique ID and ownership data, that's the moment this PS comes alive for judges who are used to seeing 2D map dashboards.

strengths: Conceptually novel relative to the rest of the land-records PS cluster this cycle.
Visually compelling if the 3D visualization is executed well.
weaknesses: Full LiDAR/point-cloud fidelity isn't achievable in 36 hours, requires deliberate scope reduction.
Narrower immediate impact case than public-facing PS in the same batch.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Weight toward visualization/3D skill, this PS's demo impact depends heavily on it.
team_fit.approach: Get a basic 3D view rendering by hour 10-12, even with placeholder data, so visualization iteration has runway.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: 3D visualization scaffolding (libraries like three.js handle a lot of this) and the ID-generation logic once the schema is defined.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing the actual ULPIN schema, what uniquely and unambiguously identifies a vertical parcel, is a data-modeling decision with real governance implications.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated ID scheme that isn't actually collision-free or legally coherent would undermine the entire point of a unique identifier system.

data_resource_availability.status: Real LiDAR/drone imagery for a specific building isn't accessible to a hackathon team; architectural floor plans are far more obtainable (sample plans, publicly available building schematics).
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Use publicly available or synthetic floor plan data for 1-2 sample buildings, clearly framed as a scoped proof of concept for the full drone/LiDAR vision.

judge_qna.question: How would this actually integrate with the existing 2D ULPIN system already in use?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your 3D ULPIN as an extension, not a replacement, each vertical parcel's ID would reference its parent 2D surface parcel, preserving backward compatibility.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens to existing 2D records during a transition to 3D?

judge_qna.question: Why floor plans instead of the LiDAR/drone imagery the PS specifically names?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be upfront: real LiDAR capture isn't accessible in 36 hours, floor plans demonstrate the same core unique-identity concept in a way that's honestly achievable, and the underlying ID logic would carry over to real LiDAR-sourced data.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would break or need to change if you swapped in real LiDAR data?
